comments.text: 15:45 as a mathematician, I agree that trials with a sample size of 1 (assuming that is what is implied with N=1 in the posts) are just nonsensical. From a statistical point of view, choosing N=1 will just yield very volatile results. Using the unbiased estimator, the standard deviation will be approximated as infinity. The smaller the sample size, the easier it is to skew the results. Sure, if the population size is incredibly small, it may be difficult to get more than 1 sample, but it is still impossible to state anything with reasonable certainty, especially when using unbiased estimators.
